summary: The Folchart Psalter is a large book of 368 pages, 38 by 29 cm, in which three scribes wrote the Psalms in gold and silver. It opens with a litany, a picture of King David as author, and a dedication naming Folchart and Abbot Hartmut. Psalm 1 has a splendid initial, and the book later warns against taking it out of St Gallen.
context: Folchart, a monk who later became prior, had the manuscript made at St Gallen between 872 and 883 while Hartmut was abbot. The litany on pages 7 to 14 names saints dear to the abbey, including Gallus, Otmar and Columbanus. Around 1545 the book was rebound, and by 1633 it was already in the library. A dedication in two lines of verse sits on pages 26 and 27.
